first rang out around 2 pm. “Iwas
on a pony, about to enter

EXPRESS NEWS SERVICE
BENGALURU, BHUBANESWAR,
THIRUVANANTHAPURAM,
LUCKNOW, RAIPUR, APRIL 22

AREALTOR from Karnataka, an
accountant from Odisha, a
Kanpur-based businessman, a
Gulf-returnee from Kerala —
among the 26 killed in the terror
attack on tourists in south
Kashmir's Pahalgam Tuesday

Prashant Satpathy, 43, from
Balasore in Odisha, who was also
on vacation with wife and nin-
year-old son. He worked as an
accountant in Bhubaneswar.
His wife Priyadarshini told
The Indian Express that he was
shot in the head when they were
alighting from a ropeway. “We
couldn’t understand what hap-
pened as my husband was sud-
denly hit by a bullet. There was
chaos all over,” she said.
A 65-year-old from Kochi in
Kerala, who was also with his
family, was another victim.
Ramachandran was on vacation

with his wife Sheela, daughter
Arathi, and her two children.
“Ramachandran was shot while
riding a horse. Later, Arathi iden-
tified the body of her father at a
local hospital,” said Jayalakshmi,
the family’s neighbour in the
Edappally area of Kochi.
Kanpur-based businessman
Shubham Dwivedi (31), part of an
11-member family group visiting
Kashmir, was also killed. He mar-
ried Aishanya Dwivedi on
February 12. “This was their sec-
ond trip after the wedding, and
this time, they chose to travel
with their families,” said

Shubham's cousin, Saurabh
Dwivedi. Shubham managed his
family’s cement business.
“Shubham and his wife chose to
goupthemountain on horseback
when the terrorists opened fire.
Shubham was killed on the spot.”
Dinesh Mirania (42) from
Raipur in Chhattisgarh, who was
visiting Kashmir with his wife
Nehaand children fortheir wed-
ding anniversary, was also shot.
“He had called me a day before.
Hesaid they visited Vaishno Devi.
Today was his wedding anniver-
sary. Hisson had joined the fam-
ily for the holiday,” a friend said.
